scope: User-approved single real-model comparison; only the resource budget profile changes. Read-only preparation except this ignored evidence artifact.

minimum_success_duration.note: Actual survival time plus final criteria held together. Sleeping cannot substitute time-of-day changes for these ticks; lower TPS requires more wall-clock time.

prior_resource_constraints.observed: Stopped after 70 requests at 432.195586 seconds, long before the 1260-second normal-TPS earliest success. Final complete-response accounting overshot the threshold to 2645103.
Was not reached in the prior run, but at its observed request rate would admit about 494 seconds of activity. Raising only max_tokens could immediately expose this next cutoff.

calibration_estimates.method: Descriptive extrapolation from one prior trajectory; not a prediction or success guarantee.
assumptions: Linear prompt-growth illustration uses prior first prompt 19085 and last prompt 51461 over 70 requests.
Actual task timing, polling, context growth, compaction, latency and environment can change consumption.

changed_only: Resource budget profile: model-call ceiling 80 to 400 and cumulative-token ceiling 2600000 to 30000000
frozen_control.initial_world_state_caveat: The same seed does not guarantee identical spawn height or coordinates. Prior initial position was [160.5, 66.0, -127.5]; inspect and retain both actual initial snapshots before interpreting the comparison.

limitations: An enlarged resource budget tests whether early cutoff was a major constraint; it does not guarantee task success.
A budget-exhausted run establishes non-completion under recorded limits, not inability under every larger budget.
Cached input is counted in the cumulative token ceiling. It is not freshly generated text and token totals do not establish monetary cost.
Prior usage was 2540416 cached-input tokens, 88693 fresh-input tokens and 15994 output tokens; 96.04 percent of total was cached input.
The observer and prompt remain frozen; inefficiencies such as repeated status polling are preserved for this comparison.
This remains one exposed dev scenario and one new trajectory, not an independent success-rate estimate.
